CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE M A CHOWDHARY, JUDGE  ORDER 01.

Applicant, namely, Himesh Kotwal, filed the instant bail application, alleging his false implication by complainant-respondent no.2 herein, to seek pre-arrest/anticipatory bail in a case registered at Police Station Janipur vide FIR No. 54/2025 on 15.04.2025, for commission of offences punishable under Sections 69, 318, 115(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.
02.

Perusal of the contents of impugned FIR would show that respondent No.2 Staffy Gill lodged a written complaint against the applicant contending therein that he made promise of marriage to her Himesh Kotwal vs The Union Territory Of Jammu & Kashmir on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163791698/
1 and they were in relationship for over a year; that under the pretext of false promise of marriage, the accused raped her on 30th March, 2025 as also on 1st April, 2025; that the accused later reneged on his promise of marriage; that on 12.04.2025, the accused physically assaulted her by injuring her right arm; that on the basis of the aforesaid complaint, FIR No.54/2025 stands registered at P/S Janipur against applicant for offences punishable under Sections 69/318(4)/115(2) BNS and investigation started in the case.
Apprehending arrest, the applicant has filed the present bail application before this court.

03. It is the case of the applicant that he has been falsely and arbitrarily implicated in a case foisted upon him, rather, it is the applicant who is the victim; that respondent no. 2, posing herself unmarried Hindu girl developed friendship with the applicant through social media as a honey trap to entangle him just to extort money from the applicant and his family; that the applicant neither extended any promise of marriage let alone false promise to the respondent no.2 nor did any wrong act with her; that when the ulterior motives of the respondent no.2 failed to fructify, she, in her frustration, cooked a false story and implicated the applicant in a case, as a result of which, FIR No.
54/2025 got registered on 15.04.2025 against the applicant at Police Station, Janipur for the commission of offences punishable under Sections 69, 318, 115(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 and investigation commenced.
Fearing threat of arrest, the applicant approached this court seeking grant of pre-arrest bail/anticipatory bail.
Pursuant to notice, objections, on behalf of the respondent no.1, stand filed.

A perusal of objections filed on behalf of respondent No.1 would show that offences under Sections 69/318(4)/115(2) BNS stand established against the applicant; that the grant of anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant has been vehemently resisted on the ground that applicant is involved in non-bailable offences, as such, he cannot seek bail, as a matter of right; that the offence punishable u/s 69 BNS carries imprisonment up to 10 years, for offence u/s 318(4) BNS, punishment is for 07 years, and for offence u/s 115(2) BNS, one year imprisonment is prescribed; that there is every apprehension that the applicant may tamper with the prosecution evidence and may even jump over the bail.
Lastly, it is prayed that relief as prayed for by the applicant in this application be rejected.

sentences.text:
Objections on behalf of respondent no.2 stand filed, inter alia, contending therein that the applicant is not entitled to bail as he has committed serious offences punishable under Sections 69/318/115(2) of BNS, 2023; that the applicant used the respondent no.2 for satiating his sexual urges by employing deceitful means on the false promise of marriage; that the applicant sent a friend request to the respondent no.2 on Instagram, proposed her for marriage and went on date with her; that respondent no.2 revealed her past of earlier marriage with one- Sweetson Gill, a child from the wedlock, disclosed fact of her second marriage to Sajid and divorce also but applicant told the respondent no.2 that he has nothing to do with her past and will marrying her and adopt her child; that respondent no.2 trusted him wholeheartedly; that upon successfully inveigling himself as true lover called the respondent no.2 at his home under the guise that he is ill and need food; that the respondent no.2 believing him went to his home and there applicant evinced his strong desire for physical intimacy with respondent no.2, upon which, she objected but applicant made her believe that they are going to marry soon, so there is no sin in doing intercourse and thus, on the pretext of promise of marriage, applicant developed sexual relations with her; that thereafter every now and then, the applicant got intimated with her; that all of sudden, applicant snapped all links of communications with respondent no. 2 and blocked her from every social media platforms; that when respondent no.2 reached Doda and contacted him, the applicant told her that he is doing this only to hide his relations and took her to Jammu in his car and told her that he will not marry her and thrown her out from his car due to which respondent no.2 received injuries upon her arm; that in the aforesaid backdrop, the respondent no.2 lodged a complaint on 15.04.2025 at P/S Janipur,
which culminated into FIR No.0054/2025 for offences punishable U/Ss 69/318(4) and 115(2) of BNS, 2023.

Lastly, it is prayed that as the applicant employed deceitful means for developing sexual relations with respondent no.2 on the pretext of marriage and when respondent no.2 asked him to solemnize the marriage, applicant snapped all links and thus cheated her, therefore, the bail application of the applicant deserves to be dismissed.

07. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the criminal proceedings launched against the applicant are nothing but a device to harass the applicant as the respondent no.2 is habitual of ensnaring the innocent people in her trap and in the present case, she threatened the whole of the family of the applicant of dire consequences and has implicated the applicant in false FIR.
He has also submitted that this court vide order dated 02.05.2025 stayed the presentation of final report/challan in the present case.

08. Learned counsel for the non-applicants argued and vehemently opposed the grant of bail in favour of the applicant in view of seriousness of the offences alleged to have been committed by the applicant and it was prayed that the application of the applicant be rejected.

09. Heard and considered.
10.
Hon'ble the Supreme Court, in a catena of judgments, has laid down principles for consideration for grant of anticipatory bail and how to exercise the power while granting bail.

In Bhadresh Bipinbhai Sheth Vs. State of Gujarat & Anr, reported as 2016(1) SCC(Crl) 240, relied by learned counsel for the petitioners, the Court while granting anticipatory bail for offence under Section 376 IPC has held:

sentences.text: "Before we proceed further, we would like to discuss the law relating to grant of anticipatory bail as has been developed through judicial interpretative process.
A judgment which needs to be pointed out is a Constitution Bench Judgment of this Court in the case of Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab [1980 2 SCC 565].

entities.text: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab [1980 2 SCC 565]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Constitution Bench in this case emphasized that provision of anticipatory bail enshrined in Section 438 of the Code is conceptualized under Article 21 of the Constitution which relates to personal liberty.
Therefore, such a provision calls for liberal interpretation of Section 438 of the Code in light of Article 21 of the Constitution.

The Code explains that an anticipatory bail is a pre-arrest legal process which directs that if the person in whose favour it is issued is thereafter arrested on the accusation in respect of which the direction is issued, he shall be released on bail.

The distinction between an ordinary order of bail and an order of anticipatory bail is that whereas the former is granted after arrest and therefore means release from the custody of the police, the latter is granted in anticipation of arrest and is therefore,
effective at the very moment of arrest.

A direction under Section 438 is therefore intended to confer conditional immunity from the 'touch' or confinement contemplated by Section 46 of the Code."
11.

The Honble Apex Court in case titled as "Ajwar Vs. Waseem & Anr"
connected with other cases reported as 2024 (6) Scale 461 in paragraph 26 held as under:
"26.

While considering as to whether bail ought to be granted in a matter involving a serious criminal offence, the Court must consider relevant factors like the nature of accusations made against the accused, the manner in which the crime is alleged to have been committed, the gravity of the offence, to role attributed to the accused, the criminal antecedents of the accused, the probability of tampering of the witnesses and repeating the offence, if the accused are released on bail, the likelihood of the accused being unavailable in the event bail is granted, the possibility of obstructing the proceedings and evading the courts of justice and overall desirability of releasing the accused on bail."
12. The factual background of the case is that the applicant and respondent No.2 had a love affair.
The non applicants have not pointed out the contravention of any of the conditions of the interim bail by the applicant after the grant of interim bail in his favour.
Without commenting upon the merits of the case, the matter for grant of bail in anticipation of arrest is to be considered.

13. Having regard to the decisions rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases referred above,
the allegations and objections filed by the Investigating Agency, lodging of FIRs by the parties against each other and considering the nature of the offences with which the applicant has been charged and also viewing that bail is the rule and jail is the exception, this Court is of the considered opinion that the applicant is entitled to be admitted to bail, particularly so when there are allegations and counter allegations which require full blown trial.

It will be in the interest of justice Himesh Kotwal vs The Union Territory Of Jammu & Kashmir on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163791698/
4 if the interim bail granted to the applicant is made absolute.

In the aforesaid backdrop of the matter, the law discussed above and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case in hand, the bail application is allowed and the interim bail granted to the petitioner/applicant vide order dated 02.05.2025 is made absolute subject to all the conditions therein.
15. The bail application is, 'disposed of' along with connected application(s).
(M A CHOWDHARY) JUDGE Jammu 25.02.2026
